body: The smell of ozone in the cellar penetrates deeper into my nostrils, a reminder of the storm’s power and its aftermath. My heart races slightly at the sight of the damaged trees outside, their branches strewn like broken dreams against the sky. I feel a protective warmth spread through me, urging me to take action. Without hesitation, I step towards the window, the glass shattering under the wind as it does every night during these storms. With each gust, I lean forward, reaching for one of the shattered pieces, pulling it back together just enough to shield myself from the elements. As the storm continues, I hold the fragile frame steady, knowing that this structure will be the only refuge I have now until everything returns to normal.
